{"id":"mimid-1wgh.37.90.2","title":"wg: pq-ciphersuites-06 L103 RFC 9420 Section 5.1.1 specifies how each scheme encodes...","description":"draft-ietf-mls-pq-ciphersuites (pq-ciphersuites-06), 2. Post-quantum KEM Cipher Suites. Editors' copy mlswg/mls-pq-ciphersuites at fb18956, L103.

Text: "The signature schemes for ML-DSA-44, ML-DSA-65, and ML-DSA-87 {{MLDSA}} are defined in {{!I-D.ietf-tls-mldsa}}."

Problem: RFC 9420 Section 5.1.1 specifies how each scheme encodes SignaturePublicKey. This draft gives no encoding for ML-DSA (raw FIPS 204 pkEncode or DER SPKI), and tls-mldsa-06 covers only the X.509 SPKI case. tls-mldsa-06 makes the FIPS 204 ctx empty only for the TLS CertificateVerify, so it is ambiguous whether MLS uses an empty ctx or carries its label there. The published -06 text is identical.

Suggested fix: Add text modeled on RFC 9420 Section 5.1.1: 'For ML-DSA cipher suites, SignaturePublicKey is the FIPS 204 pkEncode output, the signature is the raw FIPS 204 signature, and ML-DSA.Sign and ML-DSA.Verify are used with ctx set to the empty string. The MLS label is carried only in SignContent.'

Severity: medium. Verifier: narrow (tls-mldsa-06 Section 3 already settles pure ML-DSA versus HashML-DSA. Its empty ctx is stated only for the TLS CertificateVerify (line 158), and it defines key formats only through X.509 SPKI. RFC 9420 Section 5.1.1 gives a per-scheme SignaturePublicKey encoding, and this draft adds none for ML-DSA.)
